newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent bounds up, lifted by U.S. options expiry.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent bounds up, lifted by U.S. options expiry.

text.p: IPE Brent futures extended their gains by midsession Friday as fund investors sought to cover their short positions ahead of the expiry next week of the U.S. contract, brokers said.
July Brent was up 36 cents at $17.79 a barrel by 1100 GMT. July gas oil was $1.50 higher at $164 in light trade.

The Brent market was being pushed higher and could break above $19, brokers said, as players sought to cover their short positions ahead of the expiry of the front-month options contract in the U.S. during London hours.
And further buying pressure was pushing Brent higher as players covered their short positions ahead of the expiry of the July contract, dealers said.
Support also came from ongoing concerns about a delay in the second round of the Iraq/U.N. oil-for-food plan.

The United Nations on Thursday said a team of its weapons inspectors had been blocked twice from entering a total of three suspected military sites since Tuesday, adding to worries that political posturing by Iraq over the distribution of food might delay the deal.
